title: Shared Mirror edit basis with gradient-to-code generator
hypothesis: A shared physical rank-one edit atom with Givens-view logical atoms and sparse gradient-generated coefficients will represent many rank-two edits with lower N64 bytes than both MEND rank-two factors and a generic independent atom bank; a private atom should repair off-orbit edits.
physical_object: one shared rank-one edit atom plus optional private rank-one residual atom
mirror_coordinate: Givens angles for logical atoms and sparse per-edit coefficients/indices from gradient projection
logical_multiplicity: four logical edit atoms composed two-at-a-time into rank-two edits
controls: generic bank of four independent rank-one edit atoms with sparse coefficients
Mirror views plus one private off-orbit atom

task.composition: each edit sums two of four rank-one atoms with signed coefficients
task.teacher: atoms 0-2 are Givens views of one physical atom; atom 3 is independent/off-orbit
task.locality: query on inputs orthogonal to the active atom key vectors

development.selection: fixed Givens planes and least-squares gradient projection; no fresh tuning

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror+private edit NRMSE <=1.10x MEND rank-two and N64 payload <=75% MEND; without private, report the off-orbit boundary.
failure_gate: Mirror+private misses quality/byte gates, generic independent atom basis matches it at equal/fewer bytes, or locality interference increases materially.
boundaries: Analytic low-rank linear editing screen; not neural MEND reproduction.
The coefficient generator is least-squares projection from known edit matrices, an idealized upper bound.
A private atom is explicitly charged for off-orbit edit behavior.
